boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Hope College contests, ceremonies, service days and recurring campus rituals built around odd-even classes, the Pine Grove and the wider Holland community.

cards.title: Settle a Class Rivalry With 600 Feet of Rope
cards.subtitle: Freshmen and sophomores compete as Odd Year and Even Year teams
cards.notes: Watch from the designated spectator area at Buys Athletic Fields; follow the current event page for entrances and parking.
cards.short_summary: Hope’s freshman-sophomore rivalry becomes a three-hour rope contest staffed by pullers, moralers and upper-class coaches.
cards.evidence_claim: Hope College documents The Pull as a tradition dating to 1898 in which freshman and sophomore teams compete for up to three hours, with juniors and seniors serving as coaches.
cards.source_title: Hope College’s Epic Tug-of-War Set for Sept. 27
cards.access_notes: The cited 2025 contest was free and open to the public at Buys Athletic Fields-West; verify the next date and site before visiting.

cards.title: Compete in Song, Play and Oration
cards.subtitle: Even Year and Odd Year meet onstage instead of across a rope
cards.notes: Look for the annual performance announcement, then learn how each class combines an original play, group song and seven-minute oration.
cards.short_summary: A silver cup and three performance disciplines turn class-year identity into an elaborate theatrical contest.
cards.evidence_claim: Hope College states that Nykerk began in 1936 and now pits freshman and sophomore women against one another in song, play and oration, supported by junior and senior coaches.
cards.access_notes: Participation has defined student roles; consult the current Nykerk announcement for venue, audience access and any ticket requirements.

cards.title: Carry Nykerk Through Campus by Candlelight
cards.subtitle: The competition pauses for a procession to the President’s House
cards.notes: Follow the current Nykerk schedule for the service date and procession instructions; this ritual occurs during competition week.
cards.short_summary: A candlelit campus walk adds a reflective ceremony to Hope’s high-energy class competition.
cards.evidence_claim: Hope College identifies a candlelight service as a traditional Nykerk event held the week before the competition, including a candlelit campus walk with a stop at the President’s House.
cards.access_notes: The official page does not specify public access; participating students should use current Nykerk instructions.

cards.title: Announce the Next Leaders Over Breakfast
cards.subtitle: Nykerk continues the morning after the cup is awarded
cards.notes: Check the participant schedule before attending; the breakfast celebrates the competition and reveals upcoming student leadership.
cards.short_summary: The stage contest ends, but Nykerk’s leadership cycle resumes at a next-morning gathering.
cards.evidence_claim: Hope College documents the Nykerk breakfast as a traditional event held the morning after the competition to celebrate and announce upcoming leadership.
cards.access_notes: The official page does not promise general admission; follow current Nykerk participant guidance.

cards.title: Stay on Your Feet for 24 Hours
cards.subtitle: A year of fundraising culminates in one continuous dance-a-thon
cards.notes: Choose a documented role such as dancer, moraler or committee member, then use the current registration instructions before the event.
cards.short_summary: Students dance through a full day in solidarity with families served by Helen DeVos Children’s Hospital.
cards.evidence_claim: Hope College describes Dance Marathon as a year-long fundraiser culminating in a 24-hour dance-a-thon and records its first annual event in 2000.
cards.access_notes: Registration and role requirements vary; use the current Dance Marathon pages before participating.

cards.title: Take an Eight-Hour Morale Shift
cards.subtitle: Cheerleaders keep the 24-hour dancers moving
cards.notes: Register specifically as a moraler and prepare for the assigned eight-hour shift; fundraising is encouraged throughout the year.
cards.short_summary: Hope gives the support crew its own named role and sustained shift inside the marathon tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: Hope College states that Dance Marathon moralers work assigned eight-hour shifts to encourage and entertain dancers throughout the event.
cards.access_notes: This is a registered participant role; consult the current registration page and organizers for eligibility and commitments.

cards.title: Start Fall Semester With a Service Saturday
cards.subtitle: Hope students fan out to Holland-area organizations
cards.notes: Watch Volunteer Services announcements for registration and placement details, then follow the host organization’s instructions.
cards.short_summary: The fall service day sends students beyond campus to complete projects with community partners.
cards.evidence_claim: Hope College identifies Time to Serve as its fall-semester Day of Service, one of two Saturdays when students volunteer with local organizations.
cards.access_notes: Intended for Hope students; advance registration, transportation and project details should be confirmed with Volunteer Services.

cards.title: Honor Martin Luther King Jr. Through Service
cards.subtitle: The spring service day takes place annually in January
cards.notes: Register through the college when placements open, and review clothing, travel and accessibility guidance for the assigned site.
cards.short_summary: Hope’s spring service tradition connects the semester’s opening weeks with community work honoring Dr. King.
cards.evidence_claim: Hope College states that Hope Serves takes place annually in January in honor of Martin Luther King Jr. as part of its Days of Service tradition.
cards.access_notes: Intended for Hope students; confirm registration, transportation and assignment requirements with Volunteer Services.

cards.title: Turn the Pine Grove Into a Carnival
cards.subtitle: Hope marks the final Friday of the academic year outdoors
cards.notes: Head to the Pine Grove after checking the current schedule; expect the activity mix and weather plan to vary by year.
cards.short_summary: The campus green shifts into a year-end gathering of rides, inflatables, music and picnic activities.
cards.evidence_claim: Hope College documents Spring Fling as an annual Pine Grove celebration held on the last Friday of the academic year with carnival-style activities and live music.
cards.access_notes: The page presents Spring Fling as a campus celebration; verify current student access, timing and weather arrangements.

cards.title: Light the President’s Christmas Tree
cards.subtitle: Students gather at the President’s Home for Hope’s seasonal ritual
cards.notes: Check the college’s Christmas-season announcement for the invitation, date and arrival guidance before going to the President’s Home.
cards.short_summary: Hope’s president and first spouse host students for a tree lighting, carols and seasonal activities.
cards.evidence_claim: Hope College lists the Lighting of the Tree among its Christmas traditions and says the president and first spouse invite students to their home each Christmas season.
cards.access_notes: The tradition is described as a student invitation; consult the current announcement rather than approaching the residence uninvited.
